metadata.title: Supply, Demand and Equilibrium
metadata.subject: Economics
metadata.objective: Show equilibrium where supply and demand intersect and how a supply shift moves it.
metadata.learner: Can read a simple x-y graph.
misconceptions: A price change shifts the demand curve
Equilibrium means everyone can buy at any price
expectedUnderstanding: Demand slopes down and supply slopes up in the simple model.
The intersection is the equilibrium price-quantity pair.
A supply shift moves equilibrium along the fixed demand curve.
A shift of a curve is different from movement along a curve.

primitives.text: Dashed S = old supply; E slides along D
A price change moves along D; shifting S moves the whole curve.

checkpoints.title: Start at equilibrium
checkpoints.body: Demand slopes down and supply slopes up. Their intersection E is the only price-quantity pair at which the quantity buyers plan to buy equals the quantity sellers plan to sell.

checkpoints.title: Shift supply, not demand
checkpoints.body: Move the supply slider. The green supply curve shifts while the blue demand curve stays fixed. A shift of supply is a change in selling plans at every price, not a reaction to a price change.

checkpoints.title: Shift versus movement
checkpoints.body: As supply shifts, E slides along the fixed demand curve. That slide is movement along demand caused by the new price. Demand itself does not shift merely because price changed.

checkpoints.title: Equilibrium is a balance
checkpoints.body: At E, quantities supplied and demanded agree. This does not mean everyone can buy at any price: at a higher price, buyers would demand less even though sellers would offer more.

checkpoints.title: Read the new pair
checkpoints.body: A rightward supply shift lowers the equilibrium price and raises the equilibrium quantity. Follow the dashed guides to the axes: price on the vertical axis, quantity on the horizontal axis.

narration.text: Demand slopes down and supply slopes up; their crossing is equilibrium.
Shift supply and watch the equilibrium dot slide along the fixed demand curve.
A shift moves the whole curve; a price change moves you along a curve.
Equilibrium balances planned buying and selling, but it is not universal affordability.

fallback.text: A price-quantity graph shows demand sloping down and supply sloping up. Their intersection E is equilibrium: the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. The slider shifts supply horizontally while demand stays fixed. A rightward supply shift moves E down along demand to a lower price and higher quantity; a leftward shift moves E up along demand. A change in price alone moves along a curve, but a change in a non-price determinant shifts the whole curve. Equilibrium is a balance of plans, not a guarantee that every buyer can buy at any price.

accessibility.alt: A price-quantity graph: demand slopes down and supply slopes up. A slider shifts supply, leaving a dashed original supply. The equilibrium dot and dashed guides slide down along demand as supply shifts right.
